standards.name: Taxon Concept Schema (TCS)
standards.abstract: The standard addresses representation and transfer of taxon concepts (the research object) as defined in published taxonomic classifications, revisions and databases, using XML documents as the recording modality. TCS is a TDWG (Biodiversity Information Standards) technical specification comprising an XML Schema and a User Guide; it is intended to enable interoperable exchange of defined taxon concepts (either by detailing concept components or by transferring GUIDs) and to guide implementers and decision-makers in mapping their data sources to the schema.

classification.rationale: The source material provided is primarily prose describing the purpose, scope, maintenance and guidance for the schema (user guide and descriptive web page). It does not present a concrete field-level table or checklist with independently typed data fields; nor does it lay out an ordered sequence of steps. Therefore the content is best represented as a set of principles/instructions and descriptive statements rather than a table or DAG.

principles.principle: Represent taxon concepts from taxonomic classifications, revisions and databases.
principles.evidence: The TCS schema was conceived to allow the representation of taxon concepts as defined in published taxonomic classifications, revisions and databases.

principles.principle: Specify the structure for XML documents used to transfer defined taxon concepts.
principles.evidence: As such, it specifies the structure for XML documents to be used for the transfer of defined concepts.

principles.principle: Allow valid transfer documents to either (a) explicitly detail defining components of taxon concepts, (b) transfer GUIDs referring to defined taxon concepts, or (c) use a mixture of both approaches.
principles.evidence: Valid transfer documents may either explicitly detail the defining components of taxon concepts, transfer GUIDs referring to defined taxon concepts (if and when these are available) or a mixture of the two.

principles.principle: Provide a readable User Guide aimed at both decision makers and implementers, covering both general and technical topics to support implementation decisions.
principles.evidence: This guide is meant to act as a readable introduction to the Taxon Concept Schema (TCS). It is aimed at both decision makers and implementers of systems and so the content varies from being of a general nature, assuming little prior knowledge of taxonomy or XML technologies, to being quite detailed concerning the technicalities of biological nomenclature and XML schemas.

principles.principle: The User Guide is not a step-by-step manual for mapping a specific data source to TCS; implementers must make intelligent mapping decisions themselves.
principles.evidence: This document is not a step by step manual for mapping a data source to a TCS document.

principles.principle: The standard is published and maintained by Biodiversity Information Standards (TDWG) and overseen by the Taxon Concept Schema Maintenance Group.
The standard package comprises two documents: the User Guide and the XML Schema (validation schema).
principles.evidence: This standard is comprised of 2 documents.

standards.notes: Source material consisted of the TDWG standard landing page and descriptions of the two component documents (User Guide and XML Schema). The XML Schema itself (machine-readable field definitions) exists as a linked document but was not provided verbatim in the input material; extraction here is therefore limited to the prose-level statements and guidance present on the landing/user-guide descriptions.
